title.value: Type theory in human-like learning and inference
title.justification: The title was directly provided in the initial request.
title.quote: Type theory in human-like learning and inference

extractions.description: This paper explores the application of type theory in cognitive science and artificial intelligence, especially in understanding human-like learning and inference. Sosa and Ullman propose that a core component of reasoning systems is type theory, which imposes a formal structure on the computations an agent can perform. This imposition of structure helps in generating reasonable answers to novel queries, understanding improbability versus impossibility, and reasoning across varying levels of abstraction. The paper reviews empirical studies and proposes a revised model emphasizing the role of types in cognitive and program synthesis processes.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on cognitive science and artificial intelligence involving human-like learning and inference. There is no direct mention or indication that the research aims to address climate or ecologically-related sustainable development, nor is there a discussion on environmental implications.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: While understanding how people come up with new ideas, thoughts, explanations, and hypotheses that obey the basic constraints of a novel search space is of central importance to cognitive science, there is no agreed-on formal model for this kind of reasoning.
